supporting_observations.claim: The alerted transfer is visible: FILE-NWD-01 ran C:\Program Files\StratoSafe\stsync.exe as NWD\svc-archive with the Nightly job targeting ingest.stratosafe-backup.com.
The proxy recorded about 640 MB of client-to-server bytes to ingest.stratosafe-backup.com, and Sysmon attributes the corresponding proxy connection to stsync.exe running as svc-archive.
The tool, account, destination, and transfer volume match the documented StratoSafe backup explanation, which is legitimate in the environment context.

Shortly before the transfer, the domain controller recorded a Kerberos service-ticket request for svc-archive from 45.79.19.196; FILE-NWD-01 then logged a svc-archive service logon. This raises a question about the account's use, but does not establish that the external request caused the backup or transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy and Zeek records expose the destination and transfer volume, but do not establish the contents or provenance of the transferred data.
Winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable on WS-NBLAKE-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC; this is not the host generating the alerted transfer.
claims_not_established: Whether the svc-archive Kerberos request from 45.79.19.196 was authorized or how it was generated.
Whether the uploaded data consisted solely of expected backup data.
Whether the transfer was initiated as part of the scheduled backup or was triggered through misuse of the account or service.
additional_evidence_needed: Verify the source and legitimacy of the 45.79.19.196 Kerberos request using domain-controller and network perimeter records, and determine whether it was associated with authorized activity.
Review StratoSafe job and server-side audit records for the Nightly run, including the uploaded objects, job initiation, and destination account.
Confirm the svc-archive credential and service-logon provenance against the approved backup configuration and relevant change or job records.
unrelated_findings: A separate Java integration-worker process on FILE-NWD-01 connected through the proxy to receiver.citrix.com. This is not the alerted transfer; review separately without treating the unlisted service alone as proof of malicious activity. (T050-00165, T050-00249, T050-00250, T050-00251)

At 14:18 UTC, help-desk user nora.blake initiated an RDP session to FILE-NWD-01 from WS-NBLAKE-01, outside the alerted transfer window. This differs from the documented remote-administration practice and merits separate review. (T050-00441, T050-00444, T050-00448, T050-00459)
